completion_data.completion_summary: Confirmed the counter-vs-archive numbering invariant is discharged by the already-deployed membership-based allocator, declined the vault-relocation remedy with evidence in a new decision record, corrected state-write.sh's stale Check 12 cross-reference comment, and added a durable schema subsection documenting that archive numbers above the counter are expected. memory_candidates.content: state-write.sh's --allocate-into --dry-run probe requires a jq filter that actually INSERTS a new active_projects entry carrying the allocated $NAME value for the 'recording assertion' (alloc_is_recorded) to pass. A filter that only sets .next_project_number = $NAME is rejected with exit 3 ('consumed without recording it anywhere the in-use set can see'). Use: '.active_projects += [{"project_number": ($name|tonumber), "project_name": "probe", "status": "not_started", "task_type": "general"}]'. This then surfaces the separate, unrelated audit-evidence gate (exit 5) rather than an allocator refusal.

The counter-vs-archive numbering invariant in this agent system is MEMBERSHIP-based (smallest unused number across active+archive, excluding specs/vault/**), not MAX-based. An archive project_number sitting above next_project_number is an expected, correct steady state -- not a sign the counter 'lost track of' a range. Raising next_project_number past an archive maximum to 'fix' this is the wrong repair: it strands the dense free range below it. Documented in agent-system/extensions/core/context/reference/state-management-schema.md's '### Archive Numbers Above next_project_number' subsection.

Git hazard in a shared source-store repository with concurrent writers: 'git add -- <explicit files>' followed by a BARE 'git commit -m "..."' (no pathspec on the commit itself) commits the WHOLE index, not just the files just added -- it silently sweeps in any OTHER already-staged content left by a different, possibly-still-active writer. Confirmed by observing a foreign partially-staged file (status 'MM') get fully committed alongside intentional files. Safer pattern in a shared tree: pass the same explicit file list to 'git commit -- <files>' too, or diff --staged against the intended list immediately before committing.
